exposure: NIPT referral indications (e.g., normal pregnancy supervision, advanced maternal age, high risk from maternal serum screening, anxiety)
Occurrence of high-risk NIPT results (for trisomy 18, 21, monosomy X)
Timing of NIPT (early vs. late, after GW 18)
NIPT test price changes over time
outcome: Observed increase in NIPT demand (63 women for 2016-2020 vs 572 for 2021-2023)
Identification of leading NIPT indications (50.4% normal pregnancy supervision, 31.2% advanced maternal age)
Identification of common indications for late NIPT (33.3% high risk from maternal serum screening, 25% anxiety)
Prevalence of high-risk NIPT results (1.1% for trisomy 18, 21, and monosomy X)
Prevalence of fetal sex discrepancies (0.3%, 2 cases)
Frequency of common misconceptions during pre-test genetic counseling
cohort: The study included 635 pregnant women who received genetic counseling for Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT) at a Bulgarian genetic center between 2016 and 2023.
finding: The study found an exponential growth in demand for NIPT in Bulgaria, particularly as a screening method for normal pregnancies.
